DECISION. Split into 9 children: 2 new theorems (weighted_density_bound, tangent_of_weighted_tangent) and 7 comparator-accepted declarations reused by name with byte-identical frozen Lean types. Every child serves the selected statement imc_weightedTangent_iff_approxTangent. None restates it or an ancestor, and its frozen type and supplied proof are unchanged.

1. WHY SPLIT.
- The supplied proof is Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1). The printed text (book/sources/chapter-03-source.txt, lines 298-309) reads: "for every j and every x ∈ M_j ∖ E, T_x M_j exists as in Definition 1.4 ⟺ T_x M exists as in Definition 1.7, and then T_x M = T_x M_j".

- The only new mathematics is the converse "Def. 1.7 on M ⇒ Def. 1.4 on the piece" and the density bound it needs (Step 5, second bullet).
- Without the split, the selected node would re-prove several hundred lines that already exist as accepted Lean declarations.

- density_bound_of_tangent = lpf_wtc_density_bound_of_tangent: Step 5, first bullet. The accepted proof of weighted_tangent_transfer cites it as (DENSITY-BOUND). Listing it keeps every child proof closed under sibling dependencies; it needs no new work.

3. HOW THE CHILDREN IMPLY THE SELECTED STATEMENT (the selected node's remaining proof: supplied Steps 2, 3 and 7).
(i) Steps 2-3 stay in the selected node and use its existing frozen dependencies, as the supplied proof does.
- lusin_pieces (lpf_wtc_lusin_compact_pieces with V := univ, M := E) gives compact sets C_i ⊆ E with θ|C_i continuous, H(C_i) < ∞ and H(E ∖ ⋃_i C_i) = 0.

- Combine over i with ae_all_iff and pass to H⌞E with ae_restrict_of_ae. Since each C_i is closed, H⌞E((⋃_i C_i)ᶜ) = H(E ∖ ⋃_i C_i) = 0. So for H⌞E-a.e. x: x ∈ E, x ∈ C_i for some i, and (a), (b) hold at x for that i (note x ∉ E ∖ C_i).
(ii) Fix such x and i. Then:
- C_i is closed, hence null-measurable, and C_i ⊆ E;
- θ ≥ 0 on E and θ(x) > 0;
- θ is continuous at x within C_i;

(iii) (⇐) Assume HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E x Q.
- tangent_transfer with (C, N) := (C_i, E), using the densities 0 and (a), gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k C_i x Q.

(iv) (⇒) Assume HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E θ x Q.

The good set does not depend on Q, so the equivalence holds H⌞E-a.e. for all Q at once. This is Step 7, routed through Simon's printed equivalence for the piece M_j = C_i.

(a) A separate a.e. "good point" child for Steps 2-3. Children can depend only on siblings. imc_ae_zero_density_off_set is unaccepted and owned by the parent im_completeness, so it cannot be reused as a child. subproblems.title: Change of variables for Hⁿ-integrals over blow-ups η_{y,r}(S)
subproblems.statement: Let Q, n ∈ ℕ, y ∈ ℝ^Q, r > 0, let S ⊆ ℝ^Q be an arbitrary set and g : ℝ^Q → ℝ an arbitrary function, and let η = η_{y,r}, η(x) = r⁻¹(x − y). Then ∫_{η(S)} g dHⁿ = (rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_S g(η(x)) dHⁿ(x), where Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^Q and both sides are Bochner set integrals (no integrability or measurability assumption is made; the identity includes the case where both sides are 0 by non-integrability).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (y : Eucl Q) (r : ℝ) (S : Set (Eucl Q)) (g : Eucl Q → ℝ), 0 < r → ∫ z in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y r '' S, g z ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) = (r ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ x in S, g (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y r x) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted theorem: DAG node root.lipschitz_pushforward_im-a1.weighted_tangent_on_c1_chart-a1.blowup_change_of_variables-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 8389acdfdd73d9fc3fa8f08ede1aff9d04d17e88, isolated comparator passed), shared here by its Lean name with a byte-identical frozen Lean type; it is not re-proved. Its accepted parent-supplied proof follows verbatim. Inside it, 'the parent proof' means the proof of that node's original parent, and the sibling results it cites are none: it is self-contained.

Conventions: ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) = Eucl P with norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure, = μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)); on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ = Lⁿ = volume (`EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`). B̄_ρ(y) = closedBall y ρ. η_{y,λ}(x) = λ⁻¹(x − y) is `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y λ`. ∫_A f dHⁿ is the Bochner set integral (0 when f is not integrable on A); ∫⁻ is the [0,∞]-valued lintegral. 'T is the approximate tangent space of S at y' means `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y T` (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4): finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(S)} φ dHⁿ → ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ). `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T` (Def. 1.7) means finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} φ(z) θ(y + λz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(y) ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ).

This is item 0(d) of the parent proof (η_{y,r} is a similarity of ratio r⁻¹), proved for every g.

1. (η is a measurable equivalence.) Since r ≠ 0, η(x) = r⁻¹(x − y) has the inverse ψ(z) = y + r z. Both maps are continuous affine maps of ℝ^Q, so η is a homeomorphism and hence a measurable equivalence e : ℝ^Q ≃ᵐ ℝ^Q (Borel σ-algebra) with e = η and e⁻¹ = ψ. In particular η is a measurable embedding and η⁻¹(η(S)) = S for every set S.

2. (Push-forward of Hⁿ.) Put μ := μHE[n] on ℝ^Q. Claim: μ.map η = ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ) • μ. Let B be a Borel set. Then (μ.map η)(B) = μ(η⁻¹(B)) = μ(ψ(B)), and ψ(B) = τ_y(r • B) where τ_y(z) = y + z. The translation τ_y is an isometry of ℝ^Q, so μ(τ_y(r • B)) = μ(r • B) (Mathlib `Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image`). Since r ≠ 0, μ(r • B) = ‖r‖₊ⁿ • μ(B) (`MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀`). As r > 0, ‖r‖₊ⁿ = rⁿ and its image in [0, ∞] is ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ). Thus (μ.map η)(B) = ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ) · μ(B) for every Borel B, and two measures agreeing on all Borel sets are equal. (Equivalently one may use `MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image`, since ψ is a homothety of ratio r composed with a translation.)

3. (Restriction.) For a measurable equivalence e and any set s (measurable or not), (μ.map e).restrict s = (μ.restrict (e⁻¹(s))).map e (`MeasurableEquiv.restrict_map`). Taking s := η(S) and using e⁻¹(η(S)) = S (step 1) and step 2:
 (μ.restrict S).map η = (μ.map η).restrict (η(S)) = (ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ) • μ).restrict (η(S)) = ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ) • (μ.restrict (η(S))) (`Measure.restrict_smul`).

4. (Integrals.) For a measurable embedding η and any measure ν, ∫ g d(ν.map η) = ∫ g(η(x)) dν(x) for every function g, integrable or not (`MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map`). With ν := μ.restrict S and step 3:
 ∫_S g(η(x)) dμ(x) = ∫ g d((μ.restrict S).map η) = ∫ g d(ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ) • μ.restrict(η(S))) = (ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ)).toReal · ∫_{η(S)} g dμ = rⁿ ∫_{η(S)} g dμ,
 using `integral_smul_measure` (valid for every g) and (ENNReal.ofReal(rⁿ)).toReal = rⁿ because rⁿ ≥ 0.

5. (Conclusion.) Since rⁿ > 0, multiplying by (rⁿ)⁻¹ gives ∫_{η(S)} g dHⁿ = (rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_S g(η(x)) dHⁿ(x). ∎ (For n = 0 this reads ∫_{η(S)} g dH⁰ = ∫_S g∘η dH⁰, consistent with H⁰ = counting measure and η bijective.)
proof_key_steps: η = blowUpMap y r is a measurable equivalence of ℝ^Q with inverse z ↦ y + r z, so η⁻¹(η(S)) = S.
μHE[n].map η = ofReal(rⁿ) • μHE[n] by translation invariance (isometry) and euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀.
MeasurableEquiv.restrict_map gives (μ⌞S).map η = ofReal(rⁿ) • μ⌞η(S).
MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map and integral_smul_measure give ∫_S g∘η = rⁿ ∫_{η(S)} g for every g; divide by rⁿ > 0.

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent plane at a point of local finiteness gives a bounded density ratio (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3))
subproblems.statement: Let S ⊆ ℝ^Q, y ∈ ℝ^Q and T a linear subspace of ℝ^Q such that T is the (unweighted, Def. 1.4) approximate tangent space of S at y, and suppose Hⁿ(S ∩ B̄_r(y)) < ∞ for some r > 0. Then there is K ∈ ℝ≥0 such that Hⁿ(S ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ K · ENNReal.ofReal(ρⁿ) for all sufficiently small ρ > 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (S : Set (Eucl Q)) (y : Eucl Q) (T : Submodule ℝ (Eucl Q)), Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y T → (∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) (S ∩ closedBall y r) < ∞) → ∃ K : ℝ≥0, ∀ᶠ ρ in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) (S ∩ closedBall y ρ) ≤ K * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused comparator-accepted theorem: DAG node root.lipschitz_pushforward_im-a1.weighted_tangent_on_c1_chart-a1.density_bound_of_tangent-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 90ea33e846200adf6746aa4ac890fa4b8036d54c, isolated comparator passed), shared here by its Lean name with a byte-identical frozen Lean type; it is not re-proved. Its accepted parent-supplied proof follows verbatim. Inside it, 'the parent proof' means the proof of that node's original parent, and the sibling results it cites ((BLOWUP)) are the child blowup_change_of_variables of this decomposition.

Conventions: ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) = Eucl P with norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure, = μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)); on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ = Lⁿ = volume (`EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`). B̄_ρ(y) = closedBall y ρ. η_{y,λ}(x) = λ⁻¹(x − y) is `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y λ`. ∫_A f dHⁿ is the Bochner set integral (0 when f is not integrable on A); ∫⁻ is the [0,∞]-valued lintegral. 'T is the approximate tangent space of S at y' means `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y T` (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4): finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(S)} φ dHⁿ → ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ). `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T` (Def. 1.7) means finrank T = n and ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} φ(z) θ(y + λz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(y) ∫_T φ dHⁿ as λ → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ).

This is the boundedness part of Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3) (the remark at the end of item 0(e) of the parent proof). It uses the sibling result
 (BLOWUP) for r′ > 0, any S and any g: ∫_{η_{y,r′}(S)} g dHⁿ = (r′ⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_S g(η_{y,r′}(x)) dHⁿ(x).
Let μ := μHE[n] on ℝ^Q and fix r > 0 with μ(S ∩ B̄_r(y)) < ∞.

1. (A cut-off function.) Let φ₀(z) := min(1, max(0, 2 − |z|)). Then φ₀ is continuous, 0 ≤ φ₀ ≤ 1, φ₀ = 1 on B̄_1(0) and φ₀ = 0 outside B̄_2(0); so φ₀ has compact support and defines an element of C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ). Put L₀ := ∫_T φ₀ dHⁿ, a real number with L₀ ≥ 0 (φ₀ ≥ 0).

2. (Convergence.) By the tangent hypothesis, ∫_{η_{y,ρ}(S)} φ₀ dHⁿ → L₀ as ρ → 0+, so there is ρ₁ > 0 with ∫_{η_{y,ρ}(S)} φ₀ dHⁿ ≤ L₀ + 1 for all 0 < ρ < ρ₁.

3. (Comparison.) Let 0 < ρ < min(ρ₁, r/2). By (BLOWUP), ∫_{η_{y,ρ}(S)} φ₀ dHⁿ = (ρⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_S ψ dμ with ψ(x) := φ₀(η_{y,ρ}(x)) = φ₀(ρ⁻¹(x − y)). ψ is continuous, 0 ≤ ψ ≤ 1, ψ = 1 on B̄_ρ(y) and ψ = 0 outside B̄_{2ρ}(y). Since μ(S ∩ B̄_{2ρ}(y)) ≤ μ(S ∩ B̄_r(y)) < ∞, ψ is μ⌞S-integrable (bounded, measurable, vanishing outside a set of finite μ⌞S-measure), and so is the indicator 1_{B̄_ρ(y)} (μ⌞S(B̄_ρ(y)) = μ(S ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) < ∞). As 1_{B̄_ρ(y)} ≤ ψ pointwise,
 μ(S ∩ B̄_ρ(y)).toReal = ∫_S 1_{B̄_ρ(y)} dμ ≤ ∫_S ψ dμ = ρⁿ ∫_{η_{y,ρ}(S)} φ₀ dHⁿ ≤ (L₀ + 1) ρⁿ.

4. (Conclusion.) Because μ(S ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) < ∞, step 3 gives μ(S ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal((L₀ + 1)ρⁿ) = (L₀ + 1) · ENNReal.ofReal(ρⁿ) (`ENNReal.ofReal_mul`, L₀ + 1 ≥ 0). Put K := L₀ + 1 ∈ ℝ≥0. The inequality μ(S ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ K · ENNReal.ofReal(ρⁿ) holds for all ρ ∈ (0, min(ρ₁, r/2)), a set belonging to 𝓝[>]0; i.e. it holds eventually as ρ → 0+. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take the cut-off φ₀ ∈ C_c with 1_{B̄_1(0)} ≤ φ₀ ≤ 1_{B̄_2(0)}; its blow-up integrals converge to L₀ = ∫_T φ₀, so are ≤ L₀ + 1 for small ρ.

Hence Hⁿ(S ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ (L₀ + 1)ρⁿ for all small ρ; K := L₀ + 1.

Conventions.
- ℝ^Q = Eucl Q = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin Q), with Euclidean norm |·|.
- μ := μHE[n] is Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^Q. It is a Borel measure, so closed balls are μ-measurable.
- B̄_ρ(y) = closedBall y ρ and B_ρ(0) = ball 0 ρ.
- For t ∈ ℝ, η_t(x) := Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y t x = t⁻¹ • (x − y).
- φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ) means φ : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (Eucl Q) ℝ.
- ∫_S f dμ is the Bochner integral of f against μ restricted to S (it is 0 when f is not integrable on S).
- 'For all sufficiently small t > 0' means 'eventually in the filter 𝓝[>] 0'.

Fix r > 0 with μ(C ∩ B̄_r(y)) < ∞ and θ μ-integrable on M ∩ B̄_r(y). Write B_r := B̄_r(y); it is closed, hence measurable.

1. (Constants attached to φ.) tsupport φ is compact, hence bounded, so there is R > 0 with tsupport φ ⊆ B_R(0) (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_ball_lt with lower bound 0 and centre 0). φ is continuous with compact support, so there is A ∈ ℝ with |φ(z)| ≤ A for all z (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support).

2. (Choice of t.) The map t ↦ tR is continuous with value 0 at t = 0, so tR → 0 as t → 0+ (restrict from 𝓝 0 to 𝓝[>] 0 ≤ 𝓝 0). Since r > 0, tR < r for all sufficiently small t > 0. Fix t > 0 with tR < r and prove the identity for this t; that establishes it for all sufficiently small t > 0. Put F(x) := φ(η_t(x)).

3. (Properties of F.)
 (a) F = 0 outside B_r. If F(x) ≠ 0, then η_t(x) ∈ support φ ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ B_R(0). So |t⁻¹ • (x − y)| = t⁻¹|x − y| < R (as t > 0), i.e. |x − y| < tR < r, and x ∈ B_r.
 (b) F is continuous, being φ composed with the continuous affine map x ↦ t⁻¹ • (x − y). Hence F is a.e.-strongly measurable for every measure.
 (c) |F(x)| ≤ A for every x.

4. (F·θ is integrable on M.) θ is integrable on M ∩ B_r, and F is a.e.-strongly measurable with |F| ≤ A. So x ↦ F(x)θ(x) is integrable on M ∩ B_r: a bounded measurable function times an integrable one is integrable (Integrable.bdd_mul). If x ∈ M ∖ (M ∩ B_r), then x ∉ B_r, so F(x)θ(x) = 0 by 3(a). M is null-measurable, and a function integrable on M ∩ B_r that vanishes on M ∖ (M ∩ B_r) is integrable on M (IntegrableOn.of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero). Thus F·θ is integrable on M.

5. (F is integrable on C.) μ(C ∩ B_r) < ∞, and F is a.e.-strongly measurable with |F| ≤ A, so F is integrable on C ∩ B_r (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded). F vanishes on C ∖ (C ∩ B_r) by 3(a), and C is null-measurable, so F is integrable on C (IntegrableOn.of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero).

6. (Derived integrabilities.)
- Since C ⊆ M and M ∖ C ⊆ M (Set.sdiff_subset), step 4 shows F·θ is integrable on C and on M ∖ C (IntegrableOn.mono_set).
- By step 5, θ(y)·F is integrable on C.
- For all x, F(x)(θ(x) − θ(y)) = F(x)θ(x) − θ(y)F(x). So F·(θ − θ(y)) is integrable on C, as a difference of two functions integrable on C.

7. (Splitting M.)
- Since C ⊆ M, M = C ∪ (M ∖ C) (Set.union_sdiff_cancel).
- C and M ∖ C are disjoint, hence a.e.-disjoint.
- M ∖ C is null-measurable as a difference of null-measurable sets (NullMeasurableSet.diff).
F·θ is integrable on both pieces (step 6), so additivity of the set integral over this union (setIntegral_union₀) gives
 ∫_M F θ dμ = ∫_C F θ dμ + ∫_{M∖C} F θ dμ.

8. (Splitting the weight on C.) For every x, F(x)θ(x) = θ(y)F(x) + F(x)(θ(x) − θ(y)). Both summands are integrable on C (step 6), so by linearity of the integral (integral_add, integral_const_mul)
 ∫_C F θ dμ = θ(y) ∫_C F dμ + ∫_C F (θ − θ(y)) dμ.

9. (Conclusion.) Substituting step 8 into step 7 gives

for every t > 0 with tR < r, and hence for all sufficiently small t > 0. This is the claimed eventual identity. ∎

Let K ∈ ℝ≥0 be as in the hypothesis, so μ(C ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ K · ofReal(ρⁿ) for all sufficiently small ρ > 0.

1. (Cut-off.) Let φ₀(z) := min(1, max(0, 2 − |z|)). Then φ₀ is continuous, 0 ≤ φ₀ ≤ 1, φ₀(z) = 1 if |z| ≤ 1 and φ₀(z) = 0 if |z| ≥ 2. Hence tsupport φ₀ ⊆ B̄_2(0) is compact, and φ₀ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ). Put L₀ := ∫_T φ₀ dHⁿ ∈ ℝ.

2. (θ is bounded below on C near y.) θ|C is continuous at y and θ(y)/2 > 0. So there is δ > 0 with |θ(x) − θ(y)| < θ(y)/2 for every x ∈ C with |x − y| < δ (Metric.continuousWithinAt_iff). For such x, θ(x) > θ(y)/2.

3. (Choice of ρ.) Apply the weighted hypothesis to φ₀: W(ρ) := ∫_{η_ρ(M)} φ₀(z) θ(y + ρz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(y)L₀ as ρ → 0+. Hence W(ρ) ≤ θ(y)L₀ + 1 for all sufficiently small ρ > 0. Also 0 < ρ < min(r/2, δ) for all sufficiently small ρ > 0. Fix ρ with both properties. Put c := (θ(y)L₀ + 1)/(θ(y)/2) and K := c⁺. We prove μ(C ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ K · ofReal(ρⁿ) for this ρ. Since the set of admissible ρ belongs to 𝓝[>] 0, this proves the claim. Write η := η_ρ; η is continuous and |η(x)| = ρ⁻¹|x − y|.

4. (The function ψ.) Let ψ(x) := φ₀(η(x)) θ(x).
 (a) ψ = 0 off B̄_r(y). If |x − y| > r, then |η(x)| = ρ⁻¹|x − y| > r/ρ > 2, since 2ρ < r. So φ₀(η(x)) = 0.
 (b) ψ is μ-integrable on M. On M ∩ B̄_r(y), θ is integrable, and φ₀∘η is continuous (so a.e.-strongly measurable) with |φ₀∘η| ≤ 1. So ψ is integrable on M ∩ B̄_r(y) (Integrable.bdd_mul). By (a), ψ vanishes on M ∖ (M ∩ B̄_r(y)), and M is null-measurable. So ψ is integrable on M (IntegrableOn.of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero).
 (c) ψ ≥ 0 μ⌞M-a.e. Indeed μ⌞M-a.e. x lies in M (ae_restrict_mem₀, M null-measurable), and for x ∈ M, φ₀(η(x)) ≥ 0 and θ(x) ≥ 0.

5. (Lower bound.) Let A := C ∩ B̄_ρ(y). A is null-measurable (C null-measurable, closed balls measurable). Since ρ < r, A ⊆ C ∩ B̄_r(y), so μ(A) < ∞. Also A ⊆ C ⊆ M. For x ∈ A: |η(x)| = ρ⁻¹|x − y| ≤ 1, so φ₀(η(x)) = 1; and |x − y| ≤ ρ < δ, so θ(x) > θ(y)/2 by step 2. Hence ψ(x) ≥ θ(y)/2 for every x ∈ A, and so μ⌞A-a.e. (ae_restrict_mem₀). Therefore
 (θ(y)/2) · μ(A).toReal = ∫_A θ(y)/2 dμ ≤ ∫_A ψ dμ ≤ ∫_M ψ dμ.
 The equality is setIntegral_const. The first inequality is setIntegral_mono_ae_restrict: the constant is integrable on A because μ(A) < ∞, and ψ is integrable on A ⊆ M by 4(b). The second inequality is setIntegral_mono_set, using 4(b), 4(c) and A ⊆ M.

6. (Blow-up identity.) Apply (BLOWUP) with S := M, t := ρ and g(z) := φ₀(z) θ(y + ρz). Since y + ρ·ρ⁻¹(x − y) = x,
 W(ρ) = (ρⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_M φ₀(η(x)) θ(y + ρ η(x)) dμ(x) = (ρⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_M ψ dμ.
 Hence ∫_M ψ dμ = ρⁿ W(ρ) ≤ ρⁿ (θ(y)L₀ + 1), using ρⁿ > 0 and step 3.

7. (Conclusion.) Steps 5 and 6 give (θ(y)/2) μ(A).toReal ≤ (θ(y)L₀ + 1) ρⁿ. Dividing by θ(y)/2 > 0 gives μ(A).toReal ≤ c ρⁿ. Since μ(A) < ∞,
 μ(A) = ofReal(μ(A).toReal) ≤ ofReal(c ρⁿ) = c⁺ · ofReal(ρⁿ) = K · ofReal(ρⁿ)
 (ofReal_measureReal, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal, and ENNReal.ofReal_mul' with ρⁿ ≥ 0). This holds for every ρ admissible in step 3, i.e. for all sufficiently small ρ > 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Cut-off φ₀ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ) with 1_{B̄_1(0)} ≤ φ₀ ≤ 1_{B̄_2(0)}. The weighted blow-up integrals W(ρ) of φ₀ tend to θ(y)∫_T φ₀, so W(ρ) ≤ θ(y)L₀ + 1 for all small ρ.
θ|C is continuous at y and θ(y) > 0. Hence θ > θ(y)/2 on C ∩ B̄_ρ(y) once ρ < δ.
ψ = (φ₀∘η_{y,ρ})θ is integrable and ≥ 0 on M, and ψ ≥ θ(y)/2 on C ∩ B̄_ρ(y). So (θ(y)/2)·Hⁿ(C ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ ∫_M ψ.
BLOWUP: ∫_M ψ = ρⁿW(ρ) ≤ ρⁿ(θ(y)L₀ + 1). Hence Hⁿ(C ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ K·ofReal(ρⁿ) with K = ((θ(y)L₀ + 1)/(θ(y)/2))⁺.

subproblems.title: Converse weighted transfer: a weighted approximate tangent plane of M at y is the approximate tangent plane of the piece C ⊆ M (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1): T_y M as in Def. 1.7 ⇒ T_y C as in Def. 1.4)
subproblems.statement: Let Q, n ∈ ℕ and μ := Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^Q. Let M, C ⊆ ℝ^Q be μ-null-measurable with C ⊆ M, let θ : ℝ^Q → ℝ satisfy θ ≥ 0 on M, let y ∈ ℝ^Q with θ(y) > 0, and let T be a linear subspace of ℝ^Q which is the approximate tangent space of M at y with respect to θ (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T, Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.7). Assume that some r > 0 has μ(C ∩ B̄_r(y)) < ∞ and θ μ-integrable on M ∩ B̄_r(y); that θ|C is continuous at y (ContinuousWithinAt θ C y); and that θHⁿ⌞(M ∖ C) has n-density 0 at y, i.e. (∫⁻_{(M∖C) ∩ B̄_ρ(y)} ofReal(θ) dμ) / ofReal(ρⁿ) → 0 as ρ → 0+. Then T is the approximate tangent space of C at y (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C y T, Def. 1.4).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (Q n : ℕ) (M C : Set (Eucl Q)) (θ : Eucl Q → ℝ) (y : Eucl Q) (T : Submodule ℝ (Eucl Q)), NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) → NullMeasurableSet C (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) → C ⊆ M → (∀ x ∈ M, 0 ≤ θ x) → 0 < θ y → HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T → (∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q)) (C ∩ closedBall y r) < ∞ ∧ IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ closedBall y r) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q))) → ContinuousWithinAt θ C y → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => (∫⁻ x in (M \ C) ∩ closedBall y ρ, ENNReal.ofReal (θ x) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl Q))) / ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) → Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C y T
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 1, 4, 6 and 7 ("⇒") of the parent proof (Lemma B; Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1): T_x M as in Def. 1.7 ⇒ T_x M_j as in Def. 1.4, and T_x M_j = T_x M). The parent proof splits I_w(t) into θ(y) times the unweighted blow-up integral over the piece C, the continuity error on C (Step 4(c′)) and the weighted remainder on M ∖ C (Step 4(a′)). Here this is done for an arbitrary null-measurable piece C ⊆ M. The density bound for C needed in Step 6 is Step 5, second bullet; it is the sibling weighted_density_bound. This lemma is the converse of the sibling weighted_tangent_transfer. It uses the sibling results (μ = μHE[n] on ℝ^Q, η_t = η_{y,t}):
 (BLOWUP) [blowup_change_of_variables] for t > 0, any S ⊆ ℝ^Q and any g : ℝ^Q → ℝ: ∫_{η_t(S)} g dHⁿ = (tⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_S g(η_t(x)) dHⁿ(x).
 (W-DENSITY-BOUND) [weighted_density_bound] Assume: M, C are null-measurable, C ⊆ M, θ ≥ 0 on M, θ(y) > 0, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T, some r > 0 has μ(C ∩ B̄_r(y)) < ∞ and θ integrable on M ∩ B̄_r(y), and θ|C is continuous at y. Then there is K ∈ ℝ≥0 with μ(C ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ K·ofReal(ρⁿ) for all sufficiently small ρ > 0.
 (SPLIT) [blowup_integral_split] Assume: M, C are null-measurable, C ⊆ M, and some r > 0 has μ(C ∩ B̄_r(y)) < ∞ and θ integrable on M ∩ B̄_r(y). Then for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ) and all sufficiently small t > 0: ∫_M φ(η_t(x))θ(x) dμ = θ(y)∫_C φ(η_t(x)) dμ + ∫_C φ(η_t(x))(θ(x) − θ(y)) dμ + ∫_{M∖C} φ(η_t(x))θ(x) dμ.
 (CONT-ERROR) [continuity_error_vanishes] Assume: C is null-measurable, θ|C is continuous at y, and some K ∈ ℝ≥0 has μ(C ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ K·ofReal(ρⁿ) for all sufficiently small ρ > 0. Then for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ), (tⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_C φ(η_t(x))(θ(x) − θ(y)) dμ → 0 as t → 0+.
 (REMAINDER) [remainder_vanishes] Assume: D is null-measurable, θ ≥ 0 on D, and (∫⁻_{D ∩ B̄_ρ(y)} ofReal(θ) dμ)/ofReal(ρⁿ) → 0 as ρ → 0+. Then for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ), (tⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_D φ(η_t(x)) θ(x) dμ → 0 as t → 0+.
Conventions: ℝ^Q = Eucl Q = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin Q) with Euclidean norm |·|; μ := μHE[n] is Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure Hⁿ on ℝ^Q, a Borel measure (closed balls are μ-measurable). B̄_ρ(y) = closedBall y ρ. For t ∈ ℝ, η_t(x) := Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y t x = t⁻¹(x − y); for t > 0, |η_t(x)| = t⁻¹|x − y| and y + t·η_t(x) = x. ∫_A f dμ is the Bochner set integral (0 when f is not integrable on A); ∫⁻ is the [0, ∞]-valued lintegral; ofReal : ℝ → [0, ∞] is a ↦ max(a, 0) and toReal : [0, ∞] → ℝ is its inverse on [0, ∞) (toReal ∞ = 0); c⁺ ∈ ℝ≥0 denotes Real.toNNReal c. 'T is the approximate tangent space of S at y' is Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y T (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4): finrank T = n and ∫_{η_t(S)} φ dHⁿ → ∫_T φ dHⁿ as t → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ). 'T is the approximate tangent space of M at y with respect to θ' is HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T (Def. 1.7): finrank T = n and ∫_{η_t(M)} φ(z) θ(y + tz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(y) ∫_T φ dHⁿ as t → 0+ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ). 'For all sufficiently small ρ > 0' means 'eventually in the filter 𝓝[>] 0'.

1. (Dimension.) finrank T = n is part of HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T.

2. (Density bound.) The hypotheses of (W-DENSITY-BOUND) are among ours. So there is K ∈ ℝ≥0 with μ(C ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ K·ofReal(ρⁿ) for all sufficiently small ρ > 0.

Fix φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ) for steps 3–8.

3. (Weighted term after the change of variables.) For t > 0 put a(t) := (tⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_M φ(η_t(x)) θ(x) dμ(x). Apply (BLOWUP) with S := M and g(z) := φ(z) θ(y + tz); since y + t·η_t(x) = x,
 ∫_{η_t(M)} φ(z) θ(y + tz) dHⁿ(z) = (tⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_M φ(η_t(x)) θ(y + t η_t(x)) dμ(x) = a(t).
 By the weighted hypothesis, the left side tends to θ(y) ∫_T φ dHⁿ as t → 0+. The two sides agree for every t > 0, and (0, ∞) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0. So a(t) → θ(y) ∫_T φ dHⁿ.

4. (Continuity error.) C is null-measurable and θ|C is continuous at y; add step 2. By (CONT-ERROR), b(t) := (tⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_C φ(η_t(x))(θ(x) − θ(y)) dμ → 0 as t → 0+.

5. (Remainder off C.) D := M ∖ C is null-measurable, as a difference of null-measurable sets. θ ≥ 0 on D, since D ⊆ M. Our density hypothesis is exactly the density hypothesis of (REMAINDER) for this D. Hence c(t) := (tⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_{M∖C} φ(η_t(x)) θ(x) dμ → 0 as t → 0+.

6. (Splitting.) The hypotheses of (SPLIT) hold: M, C are null-measurable, C ⊆ M, and the r-hypothesis. So for all sufficiently small t > 0,
 ∫_M φ(η_t)θ dμ = θ(y) ∫_C φ(η_t) dμ + ∫_C φ(η_t)(θ − θ(y)) dμ + ∫_{M∖C} φ(η_t)θ dμ.
 Multiply by (tⁿ)⁻¹ and put m(t) := (tⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_C φ(η_t(x)) dμ(x). Then θ(y)·m(t) = a(t) − b(t) − c(t) for all sufficiently small t > 0.

7. (Main term.) By steps 3–5, a(t) − b(t) − c(t) → θ(y) ∫_T φ dHⁿ − 0 − 0 = θ(y) ∫_T φ dHⁿ. By step 6, θ(y)·m(t) agrees with a(t) − b(t) − c(t) eventually in 𝓝[>] 0, so θ(y)·m(t) → θ(y) ∫_T φ dHⁿ. Multiply by the constant θ(y)⁻¹; this is allowed since θ(y) > 0, so θ(y)⁻¹θ(y) = 1. Hence m(t) → ∫_T φ dHⁿ as t → 0+.

8. (Back to blow-ups of C.) By (BLOWUP) with S := C and g := φ, ∫_{η_t(C)} φ dHⁿ = (tⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_C φ(η_t(x)) dμ(x) = m(t) for every t > 0. Hence ∫_{η_{y,t}(C)} φ dHⁿ → ∫_T φ dHⁿ as t → 0+.

9. (Conclusion.) Step 8 holds for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q, ℝ). Together with finrank T = n (step 1), this is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C y T. ∎
proof_key_steps: finrank T = n comes from the weighted hypothesis. W-DENSITY-BOUND gives Hⁿ(C ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) ≤ K·ofReal(ρⁿ) for small ρ.
BLOWUP rewrites the weighted blow-up integral as a(t) = t⁻ⁿ∫_M φ(η_t)θ, which tends to θ(y)∫_T φ.
SPLIT gives θ(y)·t⁻ⁿ∫_C φ(η_t) = a(t) − b(t) − c(t) eventually. CONT-ERROR gives b → 0, and REMAINDER with D = M ∖ C gives c → 0.
Divide by θ(y) > 0: t⁻ⁿ∫_C φ(η_t) → ∫_T φ. BLOWUP with S = C turns this into ∫_{η_{y,t}(C)} φ → ∫_T φ, i.e. HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C y T.
